blockers.where: §6 · What would falsify this, falsifier #5 (and its one home, what_could_kill_this[4])
blockers.quote: A **third** outcome cohort with per-partner event counts in which TAF15 mortality is not elevated. The pooled crude death contrast rests on two TAF15 arms of 7 and 8 patients; a third of similar size disagreeing would put the pooled point estimate inside the comparator arm's interval.
blockers.why_wrong: The arithmetic consequence does not follow from the counts the sentence itself names. The pooled TAF15 arm is 7/15 = 46.7 %; the comparator arm's 95 % Wilson interval is 4.8–20.8 % (both printed in §3.3's own table). A third cohort 'of similar size' means a TAF15 arm of 7 or 8. The most favourable possible case — 0 deaths in 8 TAF15 patients — gives a pooled point estimate of 7/23 = 30.4 %, which is 9.6 points ABOVE the comparator arm's upper bound, not inside it; 0/7 gives 7/22 = 31.8 %. Letting the comparator arm grow with the third cohort makes it worse, not better: a Huang-shaped third cohort adding 42 EWSR1 with 5 deaths gives a comparator of 11/100 = 11.0 % (95 % CI 6.3–18.6), and 30.4 % is still outside. Solving for what would actually be needed: 7/(15+n) ≤ 20.8 % requires n ≥ 19 — a third TAF15 arm of at least nineteen patients with ZERO disease-specific deaths, more than twice the size of either existing arm and larger than any TAF15 outcome arm in the paper. As written, falsifier #5 tells a reader the headline is roughly one ordinary-sized cohort away from collapsing; the counts say it is not. The paper's own §6 preamble points at what_could_kill_this as the full list, so this is the sentence a reader would act on when judging fragility.

blockers.where: §6, falsifier #5 — and the same sentence in the artifact, what_could_kill_this[4]
blockers.quote: A **third** outcome cohort with per-partner event counts in which TAF15 mortality is not elevated. The pooled crude death contrast rests on two TAF15 arms of 7 and 8 patients; a third of similar size disagreeing would put the pooled point estimate inside the comparator arm's interval.
blockers.why_wrong: The stated falsification threshold is arithmetically false under every reading, and it understates the result's robustness by a large factor. The pooled TAF15 numerator is 7 deaths in 15. Adding a third cohort of 'similar size' (7–8 TAF15 patients) with mortality 'not elevated' gives: 0/8 -> 7/23 = 30.4 %; 0/7 -> 7/22 = 31.8 %; 1/8 (i.e. matching the EWSR1 rate) -> 8/23 = 34.8 %; 1/7 -> 8/22 = 36.4 %. The comparator arm's Wilson interval is 4.8–20.8 %, so none of these lands inside it, and the gap is not marginal. Recomputing the comparator interval after that third cohort also contributes an EWSR1 arm makes it worse, not better: adding 5/42 gives 11/100, Wilson 6.3–18.6 %, and adding 4/40 gives 10/98, Wilson 5.6–17.8 %. To bring 7/n to <= 20.8 % requires n >= 34, i.e. about NINETEEN further TAF15 patients with zero additional deaths — two to three more cohorts, not 'a third of similar size'. A reader calibrating the fragility of the headline from this bullet is misled about how much new data would overturn it, and the falsifier as written cannot be executed as stated.

Pooled TAF15 point estimates after a third cohort: 7/22=31.8 %, 7/23=30.4 %, 8/22=36.4 %, 8/23=34.8 % — all above every comparator upper bound tested (20.8, 18.6, 17.8, 19.0). 7/0.208 = 33.65, so n>=34. blockers.where: §3.3, second estimand caveat (and its stronger form in the artifact's cohort record)
blockers.quote: Second, **follow-up is unequal and, in one cohort, unstated**: Agaram's arms differ about two-fold in mean follow-up (21.7 vs 43.3 months, biasing *against* the TAF15 arm accruing events) and Huang publishes no per-arm follow-up at all.
blockers.why_wrong: The bias direction is asserted as established for a table whose headline row is disease-specific death, and for that row it is circular. These are uncensored during-follow-up proportions: follow-up ENDS AT DEATH, so a cohort arm in which 3 of 7 patients died of disease has its mean follow-up shortened BY the very events being counted. The TAF15 arm's 21.7-month mean is therefore at least partly a CONSEQUENCE of the death excess, not an independent handicap the excess overcame — so the imbalance cannot be used to argue the death contrast is conservatively estimated. (For the recurrence and metastasis rows the argument is sound, because survivors accrue observation time; the manuscript applies it to 'the table above', which includes death.) The artifact states the invalid inference outright and the manuscript's caveat is what a reader would carry away from it. Nothing in the design can establish the claimed direction for the death row without a censored (time-to-event) analysis, and §2.5 states no time-to-event quantity is estimated anywhere in this work. The honest form is that the follow-up imbalance is outcome-dependent and its net direction on the death row is UNKNOWN.
blockers.evidence: Artifact cohorts[agaram-2014-outcome].follow_up_warning: 'The bias runs AGAINST the TAF15 arm accruing events, so the death excess is observed despite shorter observation, while the recurrence comparison is confounded in the direction that produced this cohort's metastasis reversal.' | Same cohort record: strata['TAF15::NR4A3'].mean_followup_months = 21.7 with disease_specific_death {events:3, denom:7}; strata['EWSR1::NR4A3'].mean_followup_months = 43.3 with disease_specific_death {events:1, denom:16}. | Document §2.4/§2.5: 'No time-to-event quantity is estimated anywhere in this work.' | Document §4.7 restates the same pair with no direction attached, so §3.3 is the only site making the claim.

p1s.why_wrong: THE ATTRIBUTION IS CORRECT TODAY — I RESOLVED BOTH — AND NO INSTRUMENT READS IT. Exactly one committed test module opens this document (`research/manuscripts/tests/test_fusion_partner_prose_matches_its_artifact.py`; `grep -rln emc-fusion-partner-stratification --include=*.py` over the repository returns it, its two mutation harnesses, `claim_coverage.py` and `test_the_census_reads_every_publication_endpoint.py`). Its section-G identifier census matches `PMID`, `NCT` and `doi:` VALUES only (`_IDENT`); its `reference_entries` fixture reads `^\[\d+\] ` lines solely to GROUP identifiers inside an entry, and never binds the marker number `n` to a citation record. An in-text `[4]` or `[12]` is therefore not an identifier to any guard. Renumbering the reference list, inserting a reference, or retyping `[4]` as `[5]` would leave every test in the repository green while the paper credited the ≈20 % statement to a source that does not make it — which is the identical failure A11 registers for the metastasis PMCIDs and A30 for the ≈27 %. Two bindings do read the quotations themselves (`Appendix A30's verbatim quotation of reference [4]'s TAF15 share` and `… reference [12]'s`), but each binds only the digit `20` against `_ext_share(a)['percent_approx']`; the bracket number sits outside both regexes, so even swapping the two quotations' attributions passes.
p1s.evidence: research/manuscripts/tests/test_fusion_partner_prose_matches_its_artifact.py — `_IDENT` (line 1915), `_identifiers`, `reference_entries` fixture, `test_identifiers_printed_in_one_reference_entry_belong_to_one_paper`, and the two `bind(...)` calls at lines 990–996. Repository grep for other readers of this document returns no citation-numbering guard.

p1s.where: instrument coverage — PMC identifiers; the load-bearing site is §3.3 / §5 / A11 / A24, where the metastasis attribution rests on 'PMC7563993 alone'
p1s.quote: the metastasis claim attributed to a single review (PMC7563993 alone — the only actual review among the four PMCIDs previously cited for it …) **is not established by either cohort, in either direction**
p1s.why_wrong: THE ONE ANCHOR FOR THIS PAPER'S MOST ATTRIBUTION-SENSITIVE CLAIM IS PRINTED IN THE ONE NOTATION NO CENSUS READS. The guard's own comment says it: 'A PMC id is printed 23 times in this manuscript and the artifact has no `pmc` field, so a PMC id is OUTSIDE this census and is read only by `lint_citations`' provenance test.' `lint_citations.py` asks only whether `PMC\d{6,9}` is anchored in some tracked JSON — not whether it is printed against the right paper. At §3.3, §5 and A24 the review is named as 'Stacchiotti 2020, PMC7563993' with NO DOI and NO PMID beside it (the DOI 10.3390/cancers12092703 appears only in reference entry [4] and in A30), so the section-G name-attachment test, which reads only PMID/NCT/DOI within 120 characters of a citation's short name, sees nothing there. Substituting any other anchored PMCID — PMC7999686, say, which is the other review in the reference list — would pass lint_citations (anchored), pass the ownership census (PMCIDs are not censused) and pass the name-attachment test (no readable identifier), leaving the paper's single-source metastasis attribution silently pointing at a different paper. The declaration documents the gap; it does not close it. For the record, the attribution is CORRECT at the pinned commit: PMC7563993 does carry the claim, in the sentence "A slightly better distant metastases-free survival was seen in patients carrying EWS-NR4A3 compared to TAF15-NR4A3 translocation."
p1s.evidence: research/manuscripts/tests/test_fusion_partner_prose_matches_its_artifact.py lines 1911–1919 (scope note and `_IDENT`) and `test_an_identifier_beside_a_citations_name_belongs_to_that_citation` (`_NAME_TO_IDENTIFIER = 120`). research/manuscripts/lint_citations.py line 111, `"PMCID": (r"\b(PMC\d{6,9})\b",)`. PubMed Central full text of Stacchiotti 2020, doi 10.3390/cancers12092703 (PMC7563993), section 3, which contains the attributed sentence verbatim. Attribution: PubMed/PMC.

p1s.where: Appendix A, every row that states where its correction landed -- A24, A30 and A31 in particular
p1s.quote: A30: "*"below the ≈27 % the field routinely quotes"* / *"The pooled figure is below the ≈27 % the field usually quotes"* — the Abstract, §3.5, the §5 claims bullet and, as an attribution, A3 above | four sites in **this** document
p1s.why_wrong: Each appendix row asserts, in prose, the set of live sites its correction reached, and nothing derives or checks that set. A31 already states the durable lesson -- 'a correction row is the record a later round trusts, so a row whose diff does not contain its repair converts a live defect into a closed one' -- and the repair was 'check the diff against the message before committing', which is a habit, not a guard. HR-B1 is that failure recurring in the very next round: A30 says four sites and there are five. Every future correction row inherits the same unguarded shape, and the failure mode is silent and asymmetric -- a row that overstates its reach converts a live defect into a closed one and removes it from later rounds' attention. The A3 row already delegates ('the attribution itself is retracted in A30'), so a chain of rows now depends on an unverified site count.

p1s.why_wrong: The retraction round 7 performed is QUALITATIVE ('the paper does not correct the field') and every instrument aimed at it is NUMERIC. Both censuses match only fractions, rates, cohort sizes, p-values, hazard ratios and cm/months; the only instrument pointed at the retracted claim is a DECLARED_NOT_ARTIFACT_OWNED row keyed on the literal string '≈27 %', which matches nothing outside the two retained `Superseded, retained` quotations. Consequence, demonstrated by REG-B1 and REG-B2: a sentence asserting the retracted framing WITHOUT a numeral is invisible to every guard in the file, so the retraction can be reintroduced or left behind at any site and preflight stays green. The correct instrument is a forbidden-predicate assertion over the manuscript text (e.g. 'no live sentence outside a `Superseded, retained` span may claim the pooled share is below what the field quotes/repeats'), which does not exist.

p1s.quote: **I².** Not computed, for the same reason. The honest heterogeneity signal at this scale is the **range of per-cohort rates**, printed beside every pooled figure — §3.1 for the TKI-response secondary pool, §3.3 for each of the three outcome rows, §3.5 for prevalence — and computed in the artifact's `heterogeneity` blocks
p1s.why_wrong: 'The same reason' points at the preceding bullet, whose justification is explicitly scoped: 'Across the TKI-response and outcome-by-partner strata (§3.1, §3.3) the per-stratum denominator runs from three … to fifty-eight … and the event count from zero … to fourteen; a between-study variance is not estimable at that scale.' That reasoning does not cover §3.5, which is four cohorts, n = 154, 28 TAF15 events, per-cohort denominators 24/57/11/62 and a per-cohort spread of 13.4 points — a scale at which Cochran's Q and I-squared are computable and would be informative. The paper's own list then extends the no-heterogeneity-modelling decision to §3.5 anyway, and the artifact reuses the identical boilerplate note verbatim there ('at these stratum sizes a between-study variance estimate would be uninterpretable'), where it is a copy rather than an argument. This is P1 rather than a blocker because the prevalence figures themselves are right and §4.2 disclaims meta-analytic guarantees globally — but it is the analysis whose homogeneity-assuming Wilson interval is then used comparatively ('sits below the 29.2 %', Abstract and §5), which is the one place the unmodelled heterogeneity bites. An ordinary future edit adding a fifth prevalence series would inherit the same unexamined justification.

p1s.where: Abstract, §3.1, §3.3, §5 — every place a gap is printed; artifact field `comparator_minus_taf15_percentage_points`
p1s.quote: a 36.3-point gap, post-hoc Fisher p = 0.0034, and the first magnitude this contrast has ever had
p1s.why_wrong: No interval is printed on any DIFFERENCE anywhere in the paper or the artifact. Every comparative magnitude — 36.3, 9.2 and 4.3 points in §3.3, 21.1 and 37.0 points in §3.1 — is a bare point estimate, while the paper's whole claim structure is about differences and it calls 36.3 'the first magnitude this contrast has ever had'. A Newcombe (or Wilson-based) interval on the difference of two proportions is computable from exactly the counts the artifact already holds and is the natural companion to the arm-wise Wilson intervals POLICY §2.2 mandates; its absence forces the reader to reconstruct uncertainty from the two arm intervals, which is the invalid substitute the paper itself then uses (STAT-P2-3). This is P1 rather than a blocker because the gaps are arithmetically correct and §4.2 labels the pooled figures descriptive — but a magnitude offered as the paper's contribution with no stated uncertainty is one edit away from being quoted as an estimate, and nothing in the guard suite would notice.
p1s.evidence: Artifact: `comparator_minus_taf15_percentage_points` is a scalar in all six contrast blocks (analyses.A primary and secondary; analyses.B death, local_recurrence, distant_metastasis_after_presentation; analyses.B.huang_only_metastasis_readings) with no companion interval field; grep of the artifact returns no difference-interval key of any kind. | Document §3.3 table prints a 'gap' column with no interval; §5 claims bullets print 36.3 and 9.2 points with no interval.

p1s.where: research/manuscripts/tests/test_fusion_partner_prose_matches_its_artifact.py — BINDINGS construction (guard gap, P1 by construction)
p1s.quote:
# ⭐ THE UPPER-BOUND RANGE AND BOTH COMPARATOR POINT ESTIMATES IN ONE CONSTRUCTION, because the
# sentence's whole force is that the bound sits ABOVE both — checking them separately would let a
# repair move one and leave the comparison reading as though it still held.
p1s.why_wrong: The guard binds the VALUES that appear inside a relational sentence but never asserts the RELATION the sentence claims. The comment above shows the author reasoning about exactly this risk and then solving only half of it: the four numbers are read together, so a repair cannot move one in isolation — but nothing asserts `taf15_upper_ci > comparator_percent`. If a future artifact regeneration made the comparator point estimate exceed the TAF15 upper bound, the binding would still match and the sentence 'sits above the comparator arm's point estimate in both analyses' would ship as a false statement. The same hole covers every other comparative sentence in the paper: 'an interval that contains the ≈20 %' (nothing asserts 12.9 <= 20 <= 25.0 — the artifact's own `falls_inside_pooled_interval: true` is a stored boolean, not a recomputed one), 'sits below the 29.2 %', 'the pooled gap is 9.2 points with overlapping intervals', and §6 falsifier #5's 'would put the pooled point estimate inside the comparator arm's interval' — which carries no number at all and is therefore invisible to both numeric censuses, which is exactly why STAT-B2 could stand. The census tests are honest about this ('THIS IS COVERAGE, NOT CORRECTNESS'), but no other test closes it.
p1s.evidence: guard file, bind() for the upper-bound sentence (regex captures four values, lambda returns four artifact values, no inequality assertion); test_every_fraction_and_percentage_is_bound_or_declared and test_every_statistical_quantity_is_bound_or_declared both match on numeric literals only; grep of the guard for 'sits above|sits below|inside the comparator' returns only the one regex literal and no comparison logic. | Artifact analyses.C_partner_prevalence.external_reported_share.falls_inside_pooled_interval is a stored true.

p1s.quote: §3.3: 'Agaram's arms differ about two-fold in mean follow-up (21.7 vs 43.3 months, biasing *against* the TAF15 arm accruing events)' — §4.7: 'one whose arms differ roughly two-fold in mean follow-up (43.3 vs 21.7 months)'
p1s.why_wrong: The same pair is printed in OPPOSITE orders at the two sites, and neither site labels which arm is which. The only place the assignment exists is the artifact (TAF15 = 21.7, EWSR1 = 43.3). §3.3's parenthetical attaches a bias DIRECTION to an ordering the reader can only resolve by assuming first-mentioned = TAF15 — an assumption §4.7 immediately contradicts. A reader who carries §4.7's ordering back to §3.3 reads the direction backwards, and a future edit that harmonises the two orderings in the wrong direction silently inverts the paper's conservativeness argument. Both figures are numerically bound to the artifact by the guard, so the values are watched; the ARM LABEL is not, because it is never printed.

Neither sentence names an arm beside a number.
